# Planar endpoint-area comparison with an arbitrary compatible middle fiber

Let A,K,B be arbitrary planar convex bodies with

    (A+B)/2 subset K.

Consider the actual mixed source with exactly these three integer fibers at -1,0,1. It is realized by their lifted convex hull, which is a full-dimensional convex body and has no other integer bases. Write a=|A|, b=|B|, k=|K|. No centroid alignment, symmetry or polygonal structure is assumed.

If a=b, there is a deterministic point in the ORIGINAL middle fiber K whose normalized mixed halfspace depth is at least

    308/1383 >2/9.                                                   (1)

More precisely, put M=(A+B)/2 and y=g_M. The raw depth at (0,y) is at least

    (308/345)a.                                                      (2)

The ordinary centroid g_K has raw mixed depth at least (4/9)k. Selecting the better of these two proved guarantees gives (1). If k<=2a, the single point (0,g_M) has the stronger normalized guarantee 77/345.

For unequal endpoint areas, order them so b>=a and put beta=b/a. The same argument after retaining a homothetic area-a subset of B gives the explicit bound

    max_(x in K) depth_S(0,x)
       >=308/[3(346+115 beta)].                                     (3)

In particular (3) proves the planar n=1 OC bound 2/9 when the endpoint-area ratio is at most 116/115. The direct unequal-area argument in Section 6 strengthens this window to 21/20. This is a scoped theorem for three planar fibers; it is not a general OC resolution. The constants in (1)--(3) are lower bounds and are not asserted sharp.

The mechanism and split point below were developed jointly with the the contributor. It uses elementary planar section addition and two separate paired-tail lower bounds, not the false sharp linear Minkowski-excess compensation.

## 1. Paired tails at the actual Minkowski centroid

First assume a=b and put m=|M|, r=m/a>=1, y=g_M. For any nonzero u and real t write

    P(u,t)=|A intersect {u.x>=u.y+t}|
                 +|B intersect {u.x>=u.y-t}|.

There are two simultaneous universal bounds:

    P(u,t)/a >= F(r)=4sqrt(5r)/3-20r/9,                              (4)
    P(u,t)/a >= W(r)=2r/[9(2r-1)].                                  (5)

The first bound may be negative for large r, where the second remains positive.

For (4), let U,V be the two captured areas. If U+V>=a, the claim follows since F(r)=1-[2sqrt(5r)/3-1]^2<=1. Otherwise q=a-U-V>0. The Minkowski midpoint of the two complementary truncated bodies lies in M intersect {u.x<=u.y}. By ordinary Grünbaum on the opposite centroid halfspace of M, that residual region has area at most 5m/9. Brunn--Minkowski therefore gives

    sqrt(a-U)+sqrt(a-V)<=2sqrt(5m/9).

The left side is at least sqrt(a)+sqrt(q): its squared comparison follows from
(a-U)(a-V)>=a(a-U-V), whose difference is UV>=0. Thus q<=[2sqrt(5m/9)-sqrt(a)]^2, proving (4). Both residuals are positive in this case. All line boundaries have zero area, so closed complementary cuts preserve these quantities.

## 2. Width homotheties and actual section addition prove (5)

Let w_A,w_B be the positive widths of A,B in direction u, and let h_A,h_B be their upper support values. The width of M is (w_A+w_B)/2 and its upper support is (h_A+h_B)/2. The centroid support-distance bound gives

    h_A+h_B-2u.y >=(w_A+w_B)/3.                                    (6)

For a self-contained proof of that bound, normalize a body's projection to [0,1]. Homothety by s about a minimum support point places area s^2 times the whole area below level s, so its projection CDF is at least s^2. Integrating 1 minus the CDF bounds the centroid projection by 2/3. Apply this to M.

Put delta_A=h_A-(u.y+t), delta_B=h_B-(u.y-t). A supporting-point homothety proves that the corresponding cap of A has area at least

    a [clamp(delta_A/w_A,0,1)]^2,

and similarly for B. If either ratio is at least one, the full captured area a already exceeds the next displayed lower bound. Otherwise replace any negative ratio by zero; this only increases their width-weighted sum, which is at least (w_A+w_B)/3 by (6). Cauchy--Schwarz yields

    P(u,t)>=a(w_A+w_B)^2/[9(w_A^2+w_B^2)].                            (7)

This includes empty, supporting, proper and full cuts without assuming an interior minimizer.

Now align the u projection intervals of A,B by the common parameter s in [0,1]. Take Euclidean coordinates with u parallel to the first axis; scaling u does not affect the width ratios. If f(x),g(x) are their section LENGTHS perpendicular to u, the section of A+B at projection

    min_A u+min_B u+(w_A+w_B)s

contains the sum of the actual sections at min_A u+w_A s and min_B u+w_B s. In the plane these sections are intervals, whose lengths add exactly. Fubini therefore gives

    |A+B| >= (w_A+w_B) integral_0^1
       [f(min_A u+w_A s)+g(min_B u+w_B s)] ds
       =(w_A+w_B)(a/w_A+a/w_B).

The equation is written after normalizing ||u||=1; for other normal scalings the common coarea factors cancel. Since |A+B|=4m, putting R=w_A/w_B gives

    R+R^(-1)<=4r-2.                                                 (8)

Use (8) in (7):

    (w_A+w_B)^2/(w_A^2+w_B^2)
       =1+2/[R+R^(-1)] >=1+2/(4r-2)=2r/(2r-1).

This proves (5). This planar section-addition argument is independent of the normal-cone injection theorem, and it does not require a width-realizing segment to be parallel to u.

## 3. A fixed raw budget at g_M, even when K strictly contains M

Every containing halfspace may be shifted parallel to have boundary through (0,y), decreasing its measure. A nonvertical such halfspace is

    u.x+alpha z>=u.y, u!=0.

Its endpoint contributions are exactly P(u,alpha). Its middle contribution is at least the cap of the ACTUAL subset M through g_M, hence at least 4m/9. It is not being bounded by 4k/9 at this possibly different point. Thus its raw mass divided by a is at least

    (4/9)r+max{F(r),W(r)}.                                           (9)

For r in [1,33/20], the residual expression

    (4/9)r+F(r)=4sqrt(5r)/3-16r/9

is concave. Its value at r=1 is greater than one, since 12sqrt(5)>25. At r=33/20 it is

    (2/3)sqrt(33)-44/15 >308/345.

Indeed the latter strict comparison is exactly sqrt(33)>132/23, and
33*23^2-132^2=33>0. Since 308/345<1, concavity shows that this whole interval has value greater than 308/345.

For r>=33/20, the width expression

    (4/9)r+W(r)=(4/9)r+2r/[9(2r-1)]

is strictly increasing: its derivative is 4/9-2/[9(2r-1)^2]>0 for r>=1. Its value at r=33/20 is exactly

    11/15+11/69=308/345.                                             (10)

Together these prove (2) for every nonvertical cap, for all r>=1. A purely integer through-source halfspace contains the whole middle fiber and at least one endpoint, with mass k+a>=m+a>=2a>308a/345. This retains its full boundary-fiber mass. Thus (2) holds for EVERY closed ambient halfspace containing the original point (0,g_M).

The existence of the source is automatic: g_M belongs to the interior of M, and M subset K. The true midpoint centroid is used throughout. No equality g_M=(g_A+g_B)/2 is assumed.

## 4. Deterministic source selection and the equal-area normalized constant

At (0,g_K), every ambient containing halfspace captures at least the ordinary Grünbaum amount 4k/9 from K alone. Thus the maximum depth among the two actual middle points is at least

    max{(4/9)k,(308/345)a}/(k+2a).                                  (11)

Put s=k/a. The constant-over-(s+2) branch decreases, and the (4/9)s-over-(s+2) branch increases. Their crossing is

    s0=(308/345)/(4/9)=231/115.

Consequently (11) is always at least

    (308/345)/(2+231/115)=308/1383.

A deterministic rule is to use g_M when k/a<=231/115 and g_K otherwise. Both points are in the original K. Finally

    308/1383-2/9=2/4149>0.

If k<=2a, equation (2) divided by the actual total mass k+2a<=4a gives 77/345 directly. There is no transfer from a subsystem-normalized mass to the original denominator in these calculations.

## 5. A near-equal-area endpoint extension

Suppose b>=a. Choose any actual point p in B and set

    B'=p+sqrt(a/b)(B-p) subset B.

Then |B'|=a and M'=(A+B')/2 is contained in K. Applying the fixed RAW estimate (2) to A,B',K gives a point g_(M') in the original K with raw depth at least (308/345)a for that subsystem. Every additional point of B has nonnegative measure in every containing cap, so the SAME point has at least that raw depth in the original source A,K,B. Independently g_K still has raw depth at least 4k/9. The true denominator is now a+b+k, giving

    max depth >=max{(4/9)k,(308/345)a}/(k+a+b).

As a function of k/a, the two branches again meet at 231/115, and their opposite monotonicities give the universal lower bound

    308/[3(346+115 b/a)].

It is at least 2/9 exactly when b/a<=116/115. Interchanging the endpoints handles the opposite order. The homothety retains a positive planar convex body and uses an actual point p; no optimization of that choice, rationality assumption or limiting construction is involved.

## 6. Direct unequal-area comparison: endpoint ratio up to 21/20

The endpoint-subset argument loses some useful unequal-volume information. Retaining BOTH actual bodies yields the following stronger conclusion:

    1<=beta=b/a<=21/20  ==>  some actual point of K has depth>2/9.    (12)

Put M=(A+B)/2, m=|M|, r=m/a and y=g_M. Brunn--Minkowski gives

    r>=r_min=(1+sqrt(beta))^2/4>=1.

The following two bounds hold for the actual paired mass P(u,t):

    P/a >= F_beta(r)=1-beta-20r/9+(4/3)sqrt(5beta r),                (13)
    P/a >= W(r)=2r/[9(2r-1)].                                      (14)

To prove (13), the case P>=a is immediate since F_beta=1-[2sqrt(5r)/3-sqrt(beta)]^2<=1. Otherwise write U+V=P<a, with U captured from A and V from B. Among the two residual square roots with U+V=P, concavity minimizes their sum at U=0 or U=P. Since b>=a, the smaller endpoint is

    sqrt(a-P)+sqrt(b).

One direct comparison uses the decreasing function sqrt(x)-sqrt(x-P) for x>P. The same residual-midpoint and ordinary centroid bound as before then give

    sqrt(a-P)+sqrt(b)<=2sqrt(5m/9).

Rearranging proves (13). In the current parameter range its right-hand root difference is positive, since 20r>=20>9beta. No squaring with an unknown sign is used.

For (14), the two supporting-point cap homotheties give areas at least a times the sum of their squared clipped ratios, because b>=a. The Cauchy argument in (7) is therefore still valid with coefficient a. Also the actual section-addition inequality is

    4m>=(w_A+w_B)(a/w_A+b/w_B)
         >=a(w_A+w_B)(1/w_A+1/w_B).

Consequently R+R^(-1)<=4r-2 still follows. This proves (14) for the unequal pair with no body deletion and the original cap orientations.

If k>=a+b, the ordinary middle centroid alone gives the required bound, and it is strict when k>a+b. It therefore remains to treat k<=a+b. Then

    r_min<=r<=k/a<=1+beta.

At (0,g_M) the own contribution from its actual subset M is at least (4/9)m. It suffices to show that

    (4/9)r+max{F_beta(r),W(r)}>(4/9)(1+beta),                        (15)

because (4/9)(a+b)>=(2/9)(a+b+k).

Choose the exact moving split

    r_split=(19beta+14)/20.

It lies strictly between r_min and 1+beta: r_min<=beta and r_split>beta, while r_split<1+beta. On [r_min,r_split] the residual difference in (15), multiplied by nine, is

    G_beta(r)=12sqrt(5beta r)-16r+5-13beta.

It is concave in r. At r_min, use r_min<=beta<=21/20 and sqrt(5beta r_min)>=sqrt(5)>11/5 to obtain

    G_beta(r_min)>132/5+5-29(21/20)=19/20>0.

At the split its positivity is

    6sqrt(beta(19beta+14))>(141beta+31)/5.

Both sides are positive, and their squared difference times 25 is

    -2781beta^2+3858beta-961.

This concave polynomial has values 116 at beta=1 and 9539/400 at beta=21/20, both positive. It is therefore positive throughout the interval. Concavity in r now proves the residual part of (15) on the whole lower r interval.

On [r_split,infinity), the function (4/9)r+W(r) is strictly increasing, as already proved. At the split, its difference from (4/9)(1+beta) is exactly

    [46-23beta-19beta^2]/[45(19beta+4)].                              (16)

The numerator is decreasing for beta>0, and at beta=21/20 it equals 361/400>0. This proves the width part of (15) for every r>=r_split. Thus (15) holds throughout the only nonheavy-middle regime.

Purely integer halfspaces at (0,g_M) contain K and an endpoint, of total mass at least k+a. Since k>=m>=a and beta<=21/20,

    k+a >=2a > (4/9)(a+b),

so they also satisfy the stated sufficient raw budget. Closed halfspace boundary mass is therefore retained here as well. The point g_M is an actual point of K. Combining this with g_K in the heavy-middle case proves (12), with no centroid alignment, approximation, or optimized contraction choice.
